Team —

We need to lock final OKR scores and collect supporting evidence for the QBR packet by EOD today. BrightWire (Jamie) has submitted partial evidence but flagged two metrics that need reconciled numbers (see note below). Proposed plan:

- Everyone to confirm final score + 1-line rationale in reply
- Upload evidence pieces to the "OKR Evidence 2027" Drive folder (link below) and drop filenames here
- I'll assemble the QBR narrative draft and circulate for a single pass at 3pm PT

Contested metrics (from BrightWire):
- SLO adoption rate (customer-side) — discrepancy between PM tracking vs. customer-reported config counts
- Average inference spend per 100k tokens — accounting shows a higher delta for May (need raw billing export)

Attachments for intake: Q3_OKR_Evidence.xlsx (template)
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/okr-evidence-2027

Thanks,
Mateo

> We need to lock final OKR scores...

Locking my scores now. Quick notes:
- Objective: "Reduce unit inference cost by 20%" — Final score: 0.6 (partial). Rationale: quantization experiments hit ~12% cost reduction in prod but large-traffic models still need KV-cache tuning. Evidence uploaded: Q3_OKR_Evidence.xlsx -> sheet "Cost-Perf" and "quant-exp-results.csv" (Attachment stub).
- For the BrightWire SLO adoption discrepancy — I validated their config snapshot and we have a mismatch because their customer disabled telemetry for a subset of accounts in May. I attached the telemetry opt-out log.

Attachment: quant-exp-results.csv (csv), telemetry-optout-log.txt (txt)

—Laura

VP, Customer Reliability

-Vivek

> Two quick items:
> 1) ...
>
I've pulled the evidence and drafted the narrative wedge for the "Cost" objective. Proposed text (copy for QBR):

"We realized measurable unit-cost reductions through targeted quantization and workload-aware batching. Net reduction reached 12% across pilot clusters; however, traffic composition and KV-cache tuning limited savings for several high-throughput models. We recommend a Q3 initiative to automate KV-cache profiling and expand quantization to the top 10 traffic models. (See evidence: quant-exp-results.csv; billing-reconciled-may.csv)"

If everyone is fine with that phrasing I can drop it into the master draft and run a single grammar pass at 3pm. Also, I recommend we annotate BrightWire's SLO metric as 'customer-count (reported)' and call out telemetry opt-out in a footnote.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Marketing

Thanks everyone — this is the closeout.

Decisions and next steps (finalize by EOD):
- Scores locked as follows (final): Cost objective = 0.6 (partial), Reliability objective = 0.8, Adoption objective = 0.7 (customer-reported; footnote re: telemetry opt-out)
- Evidence files to include in packet: quant-exp-results.csv, telemetry-optout-log.txt, billing-reconciled-may.csv, brightwire_billing_export_may.csv
- Narrative: Marissa will merge her wedge into QBR_narrative_draft.md and circulate by 15:00 PT for a single-pass edit.
- Finance/Operations (Vivek & Ben): finalize the reconciled billing CSV and provide score_change_log.csv for audit trail.
- Legal/Procurement: CC'd Atlas Cloud procurement to confirm procurement playbook mention in QBR (procurement@atlascloud.com)

I've attached the intake template with filenames flagged: Q3_OKR_Evidence.xlsx. Final QBR doc link: https://docs.redwood.com/d/qbr-narrative-draft

If there are no objections by 3pm I'll send the packet to Exec Comms for distribution on Monday.

Mateo
